experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route that winds through the most spectacular landscapes of Torres del Paine, including the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the base of the iconic Torres towers. Stay in mountain refugios or camp along the way for a true Patagonian adventure.
experiences.location: W Circuit, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Set out before dawn to hike to the base of the three iconic granite towers of Torres del Paine. Arrive at the glacial lagoon at sunrise to witness the towers bathed in golden and pink light reflecting off the turquoise water — one of the most breathtaking natural spectacles in South America.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the stunning blue ice walls of one of Patagonia's most impressive glaciers, offering a unique perspective impossible to get on foot.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Grey Glacier Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Trekking Day
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, towering granite walls, and the peaks of Cuernos del Paine. Listen for the thunderous crack of ice avalanches cascading down the mountainsides as you trek through this awe-inspiring natural amphitheater.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari
experiences.description: Join an expert naturalist guide on a dedicated wildlife tracking excursion through the park's open pampas and valleys. Torres del Paine is one of the best places on Earth to spot wild pumas, guanacos, Andean condors, and rheas in their natural habitat. Early morning and dusk offer the highest chances of sightings.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Pampas, Northern Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and arrange shared transfer or budget bus to Puerto Natales (approx. 3-4 hours). Check in to a budget hostel in Puerto Natales for the night to rest before entering the park.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Puerto Natales waterfront (Seno Ultima Esperanza). Visit a local gear shop to confirm equipment rentals and buy any last-minute trekking supplies. Pick up park permits and confirm campsite/refugio bookings for the W Circuit.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport café
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich from a bakery in Puerto Natales after arrival — La Mesita Grande or a local panadería (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Aldea Restaurant or Afrigonia in Puerto Natales — budget set menu (menú del día) for ~$10-12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book shared transfers in advance to save costs. Confirm all CONAF park reservations online before arrival. Puerto Natales is the last chance to stock up on affordable food supplies for the trail — buy snacks, instant meals, and energy bars at a local supermarket (Unimarc or Multiahorro).

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast in Puerto Natales. Board the budget bus or shared van to Torres del Paine National Park (Laguna Amarga entrance). Depart by 07:30 to maximize daylight. Pay park entrance fee (~$35 USD for foreigners in peak season).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the park and take the free ferry across Lago Pehoe or the bus to the starting point of the W Circuit at the eastern end (Las Torres sector). Check in to Refugio Las Torres or designated campsite. Set up camp if tenting. Take a short acclimatization walk along the Río Ascencio valley to stretch legs after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp/refugio. Cook a simple pasta or rice meal on a camp stove using supplies bought in Puerto Natales. Review maps and trail notes for the next day's sunrise hike. Sleep early — wake-up will be before 04:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared oats or bread with jam at hostel in Puerto Natales (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus — sandwiches and fruit prepared the night before
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp meal: pasta with tuna and olive oil (~$3-4 USD using trail supplies)

day_by_day.notes: The bus from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine departs around 07:30 from the bus terminal. Book in advance during December (peak season). Refugio Las Torres has a paid kitchen area; campers must bring their own stove and fuel. Set multiple alarms for the sunrise hike.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — Wake up at 03:30 and begin hiking by 04:00 in darkness with headlamps. Trek 9 km uphill through lenga beech forest and rocky moraine to reach the base of the iconic granite towers (Mirador Las Torres) at sunrise (~06:30-07:00). Witness the famous alpenglow on the three towers reflected in the turquoise glacial lake below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Refugio Las Torres by midday. Rest, eat lunch, and rehydrate. In the afternoon, take a leisurely walk along the Río Ascencio to explore the lower valley and spot Andean condors soaring overhead.
day_by_day.evening: Rest tired legs at camp. Cook a hearty dinner. Journal or stargaze — December nights in Patagonia have very long daylight (sunset around 22:00), so enjoy the extended golden hour light on the surrounding peaks.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed energy bars and trail mix eaten on the hike before dawn
meals.lunch: Hot soup and bread at Refugio Las Torres cafeteria (~$8-10 USD) or self-cooked instant soup at camp
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp meal: lentil soup with crackers and cheese (~$3-4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise hike is 18 km round trip with 800m elevation gain — allow 5-6 hours total. Bring extra warm layers as temperatures near the mirador can be near freezing at dawn even in December. This is the highlight experience of the W Circuit — weather permitting, clear mornings are most common in early December. Trekking poles strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the W Circuit westward leg. Trek from Las Torres sector toward Refugio Los Cuernos (approx. 11 km, 3-4 hours). The trail follows the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld with dramatic views of the Cuernos del Paine (Horns of Paine) — some of the most photogenic peaks in the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos by early afternoon. Check in to campsite or dorm. Explore the shoreline of Lago Nordenskjöld and photograph the turquoise water against the jagged Cuernos peaks. Optional short side trail to a viewpoint above the refugio.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views over Lago Nordenskjöld are spectacular — the Cuernos glow orange and red. Cook dinner at camp and socialize with fellow trekkers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked oatmeal with dried fruit at Las Torres camp before departing
meals.lunch: Trail snacks eaten while hiking — nuts, energy bars, dried mango (~$2 USD from supplies)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp meal: rice with dehydrated vegetables and soy sauce (~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a moderate hiking day — a good recovery day after the strenuous sunrise hike. The trail is well-marked. Lago Nordenskjöld is one of the most beautiful lakes in the park. Bring a camera with extra battery as charging options are limited (some refugios offer paid charging).

day_by_day.morning: Valle del Francés Trekking Day — Start early from Los Cuernos and trek into the Valle del Francés, one of the most dramatic glacially carved valleys in Patagonia. The trail climbs steeply through lenga beech forest with increasingly spectacular views of hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and towering granite walls on both sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to Mirador Británico (the upper viewpoint) at approximately 1,100m elevation — the highest point of the W Circuit and arguably the most breathtaking panoramic view in the entire park. On clear days you can see Glacier del Francés calving ice into the valley below. Descend back to Campamento Italiano at the valley entrance.
day_by_day.evening: Trek back to Refugio Paine Grande (approx. 5 km from Campamento Italiano along the lake shore). Check in to the campsite or dorm at Paine Grande. This is the largest refugio on the circuit with better facilities.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked oatmeal and coffee at Los Cuernos before the big hiking day
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mirador Británico — sandwiches, cheese, and chocolate (~$2-3 USD from supplies)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to the refugio cafeteria at Paine Grande — hot meal such as soup and empanadas (~$12-15 USD) after a very long day

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés day is approximately 20-22 km round trip with significant elevation gain — the longest and most demanding day of the W Circuit. Start by 07:00. Leave heavy packs at Campamento Italiano (free bag drop area). Watch for falling ice and rocks in the upper valley — do not approach glacier edges. Weather can change rapidly; pack full rain gear.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at Refugio Paine Grande. Sleep in slightly, do laundry (hand wash), and tend to any blisters or muscle soreness. Short optional walk to the shore of Lago Pehoé to admire views of the Paine Massif reflected in the vivid turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the catamaran across Lago Pehoé to Pudeto (approx. 30-minute ride, ~$25 USD — budget for this essential crossing). From Pudeto, either hike or take the park bus toward Lago Grey sector. Begin the trek toward Refugio Grey along the western arm of the W Circuit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Grey campsite. Set up camp with views of the massive Glacier Grey — one of the largest glaciers in the Southern Patagonian Ice Field visible from the trail. Watch the glacier in the long evening light.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked breakfast at Paine Grande — instant coffee, crackers with peanut butter
meals.lunch: Snacks and trail food during the catamaran and afternoon hike
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp meal at Refugio Grey: instant mashed potatoes with canned sardines (~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Lago Pehoé catamaran schedule is fixed — check times in advance (typically departs Paine Grande at 09:30 and 18:00 in peak season). Book the catamaran ticket in advance online or at the refugio reception. The western W Circuit leg to Glacier Grey is less crowded than the eastern section.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Grey Exploration Day — Hike the trail from Refugio Grey northward to Mirador Glacier Grey for close-up views of the massive blue glacier face and floating icebergs in Lago Grey. The glacier is approximately 6 km wide and 30 km long — one of the most impressive in South America accessible on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Refugio Grey. Optional: rent a kayak near the refugio to paddle among icebergs on Lago Grey (~$30-40 USD for 2 hours — a worthwhile splurge if budget allows). Alternatively, take the free trail to a second viewpoint south of the refugio for different glacier perspectives.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return hike back toward Pudeto or stay a second night at Refugio Grey. Enjoy the midnight-like golden hour sunset (around 22:00) over the glacier — one of the most magical light shows in Patagonia.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked oatmeal at Refugio Grey camp
meals.lunch: Packed trail snacks at Mirador Glacier Grey viewpoint
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp meal: pasta with pesto sauce packet and parmesan (~$3-4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the westernmost point of the W Circuit. Glacier Grey has been retreating significantly due to climate change — the current ice face is several kilometers from where it was 20 years ago. The blue icebergs floating in Lago Grey are extraordinary. Bring polarized sunglasses as glacial glare is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Complete the W Circuit return leg — hike back from Refugio Grey toward Pudeto (approx. 11 km, 3-4 hours). The trail passes through open Patagonian steppe with guanacos often visible grazing near the path. Take the catamaran back across Lago Pehoé to Paine Grande if not already done.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the park bus from the Paine Grande/Pudeto area to the Administration Center (Guardería) near Lago del Toro. Visit the CONAF park administration center and small free museum about the park's ecology, geology, and conservation history. Walk the short nature trail near the administration center.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to budget accommodation near the park administration or Hostería Las Torres area. Celebrate completing the W Circuit with a slightly better dinner. Hot shower — a luxury after days of camp life.

meals.breakfast: Final self-cooked camp breakfast — use up remaining trail supplies
meals.lunch: Snacks during the return hike
meals.dinner: Hostería Las Torres restaurant or park cafeteria — budget set menu (~$15-18 USD as a post-trek celebration)

day_by_day.notes: Finishing the W Circuit typically takes 4-5 days; this itinerary builds in extra time for flexibility and weather delays — common in Patagonia. Use any extra time at the administration center to report any trail conditions or wildlife sightings to CONAF rangers. Begin planning the return transfer to Puerto Natales.

day_by_day.morning: Day hike to Mirador Condor and the Laguna Verde area near the park's southern sector — a less-visited trail offering solitude and excellent birdwatching. Look for Andean condors, black-necked swans, flamingos in the lagoon, and the endemic Patagonian fox.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take the park bus along the main park road to Lago Sarmiento viewpoints. Stop at Salto Grande waterfall — a powerful waterfall connecting Lago Nordenskjöld to Lago Pehoé, easily accessible from the road and free to visit. Excellent photography spot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Pack gear and prepare for the next day's excursion. Hand-wash hiking clothes and dry them in the long evening light. Review photos from the W Circuit.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or refugio breakfast if included, or self-cooked
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Laguna Verde (~$2-3 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal or budget cafeteria option (~$8-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Salto Grande is one of the most accessible and impressive waterfalls in the park — reachable in a 10-minute walk from the road. Laguna Verde and Laguna Amarga in the eastern park are important flamingo habitats — bring binoculars. The eastern park road passes through open steppe where guanaco sightings are nearly guaranteed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk around Laguna Amarga — the salt lagoon near the eastern park entrance is a prime flamingo feeding area, especially in morning hours when winds are calm. Also watch for rheas (Darwin's rhea — the Patagonian ostrich) and upland geese on the open steppe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the park bus back to Puerto Natales. Arrive in the afternoon and check in to a budget hostel. Rest, shower thoroughly, and do laundry. Explore the Puerto Natales town center — visit the Museo Histórico Municipal (free) and the local artisan market for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner in Puerto Natales — many local restaurants offer a special holiday set menu. Enjoy a proper sit-down meal with Patagonian lamb (cordero al palo) if budget allows — a regional specialty worth trying once.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked or hostel breakfast before departing the park
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus back to Puerto Natales
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special at a local Puerto Natales restaurant — Patagonian lamb or seafood set menu (~$18-22 USD as a holiday splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve (Nochebuena) is celebrated warmly in Chilean Patagonia. Some restaurants may be fully booked — reserve in advance. The bus from the park to Puerto Natales typically departs in the afternoon. Laguna Amarga flamingo viewing is best in calm morning conditions before the notorious Patagonian wind picks up.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — Relaxed morning in Puerto Natales. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the waterfront Costanera for a morning walk along Seno Ultima Esperanza (Last Hope Sound) — named by early Spanish explorers. Watch for dolphins and black-necked cormorants in the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day excursion to Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument (about 24 km from Puerto Natales, ~$8 USD entrance). This large cave housed a giant ground sloth (Mylodon) 10,000 years ago — fascinating paleontology site with a life-size replica. Accessible by taxi (~$15-20 USD round trip shared) or organized budget tour.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Puerto Natales. Browse the artisan market for last-minute souvenirs — handmade wool products, local jams, and Patagonian crafts. Pack bags for departure the next day.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café — medialunas (croissants) and coffee (~$3-4 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Puerto Natales café — empanadas and fresh juice (~$6-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at El Rincón de los Viajeros or similar backpacker-friendly restaurant in Puerto Natales (~$10-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Many businesses in Puerto Natales may be closed or have limited hours on Christmas Day — stock up on food the day before. Cueva del Milodón is one of the most underrated attractions in the region and far less crowded than Torres del Paine. Combine with 1-2 other travelers to share taxi costs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Early breakfast and check out of hostel. Last walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront for final views of the Patagonian fjords and mountains. Pick up any remaining souvenirs or local products (mermelada de calafate — calafate berry jam is the classic edible souvenir).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take shared transfer or bus to Punta Arenas airport (approx. 3-4 hours). Depart Puerto Natales by 08:00-09:00 to ensure comfortable arrival at the airport for afternoon or evening flights. Check in for departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Punta Arenas. Reflect on 12 extraordinary days in one of the world's most spectacular wilderness areas — the W Circuit completed, glaciers witnessed, condors spotted, and the iconic Torres del Paine seen at sunrise.

meals.breakfast: Final hostel breakfast or café in Puerto Natales — make it count (~$4-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Airport café in Punta Arenas or packed sandwich for the bus journey (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer booking the day before departure. Punta Arenas airport (PUQ) is the main regional hub — allow at least 2 hours before flight departure. If time allows at Punta Arenas airport, the city center is 15 minutes away and worth a quick visit to Plaza Muñoz Gamero and the famous Magellanic penguin colony at Reserva Pingüino Rey (if day permits). The calafate berry is a Patagonian legend — eating it guarantees you will return to Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange pre-booked transfer to Puerto Natales.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Puerto Natales (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hostel in Puerto Natales for the night. Stroll along the Ultima Esperanza Sound waterfront, visit the local artisan market, and pick up any last-minute trekking supplies at Erratic Rock or Base Camp outdoor stores.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free 3pm (or 7pm) trekking orientation talk at Erratic Rock hostel — a legendary Patagonia institution that briefs hikers on W Trek logistics, gear, and conditions. Review your packing list and prepare gear for the multi-day trek ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Quick empanadas or sandwich from a local bakery near the Puerto Natales bus terminal upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Afrigonia Restaurant in Puerto Natales — a beloved mid-range spot blending Patagonian lamb and seafood with global flavors. Budget ~$18–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your park entrance reservation and CONAF camping/refugio bookings tonight. Ensure you have Chilean pesos for park fees and small vendors. Pack rain layers, gaiters, and a headlamp for the trek starting tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast then board the 7:30am catamaran or bus transfer from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine National Park (approx. 2.5–3 hours). Enter the park, pay entrance fee (~$35 USD in peak season), and transfer to the Laguna Amarga ranger station. Begin the W Trek Multi-Day Hike from the eastern entrance, hiking toward Las Torres base camp (approx. 4–5 hours, 9km with 700m elevation gain).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Refugio Las Torres (formerly Chileno) area by early afternoon. Check in, claim your bunk or tent pitch, and rest tired legs. Take a short exploratory walk around Laguna Torres to admire the first dramatic views of the granite towers and turquoise glacial lake.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the refugio atmosphere, meet fellow trekkers, and dry any damp gear. Enjoy the long Patagonian summer daylight (sunset around 10pm) with views of the towers glowing in alpenglow light.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your Puerto Natales accommodation before departure — eggs, toast, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared the night before or purchased at the park entrance kiosk — sandwich, fruit, energy bars
meals.dinner: Hot dinner at Refugio Las Torres dining room — set menu typically includes soup, main (pasta or lamb stew), and dessert. Budget ~$25–30 USD. Vegetarian options usually available.

day_by_day.notes: This is Day 1 of the W Trek. Pace yourself on the ascent — the trail gains significant elevation in the final stretch. Trekking poles strongly recommended. December weather can bring afternoon wind and rain; keep rain gear accessible in your daypack.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — wake at 4:30am and set out by 5:00am with headlamps for the iconic pre-dawn hike to the base of the Torres (approx. 2.5 hours up from Refugio Chileno, or 1 hour from the upper camp). Arrive at Laguna Torres at sunrise to witness the three granite monoliths bathed in golden-pink light reflecting in the still glacial lake — one of Patagonia's most breathtaking spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Refugio Las Torres, collect your full pack, and begin trekking westward along the W route toward Valle del Francés. Hike through open lenga beech forest with condor sightings common overhead. Reach Refugio Los Cuernos by mid-to-late afternoon (approx. 11km, 3–4 hours from Torres camp).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos with stunning views of Lago Nordenskjöld and the dramatic Cuernos del Paine peaks. Rest, stretch, and journal about the day's extraordinary sunrise experience.

meals.breakfast: Energy bars and thermos coffee consumed on the trail before sunrise — pack the night before
meals.lunch: Hot meal back at Refugio Las Torres after descending from the towers, before continuing trek — soup and sandwich
meals.dinner: Set dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos — hearty Patagonian fare with lake views. Budget ~$25–30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most photographed moment in Patagonia — worth every early alarm. Bring a tripod if you carry one. The lake surface is calmest in the early morning before wind picks up. Weather permitting, the reflection of the towers in the lake is surreal.

day_by_day.morning: Valle del Francés Trekking Day — depart Refugio Los Cuernos early and hike into the spectacular Valle del Francés (approx. 3–4 hours to the upper mirador). This glacially carved valley is flanked by hanging glaciers, dramatic waterfalls, and towering granite walls. Listen for the thunderous crack of ice calving from Glaciar del Francés above. Hike to Mirador Británico (the upper viewpoint) for a 360-degree panorama of peaks, glaciers, and the valley below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the valley and continue trekking west toward Campamento Italiano and then onward to Refugio Paine Grande on the shores of Lago Pehoé (approx. 5–6 hours total for the full valley day). Arrive at Paine Grande by late afternoon — the largest refugio on the W Trek with a lively atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate reaching the midpoint of the W Trek with fellow hikers. Watch the evening light paint the Paine Massif in shades of orange and purple from the refugio's lakeside deck.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos before departure — porridge, eggs, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mirador Británico or Campamento Italiano — sandwiches, nuts, chocolate
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Paine Grande restaurant — pasta, soup, and local craft beer available. Budget ~$25–30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is considered by many trekkers the most dramatic section of the W Trek. Keep eyes skyward for Andean condors riding thermals above the valley walls. The upper section of the trail may have snow in December — trekking poles essential.

day_by_day.morning: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — depart Refugio Paine Grande early and join a guided kayaking excursion on Lago Grey (pre-booked, approx. $120–150 USD per person). Paddle through icy aquamarine waters surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier — one of the largest glaciers in Patagonia outside of Antarctica. Your expert guide explains glaciology, climate change impacts, and local ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue paddling toward the glacier face for close-up views of the 30-meter-high blue ice walls. Return to shore by early afternoon. Dry off, warm up with hot drinks, and begin the final western leg of the W Trek hiking toward Refugio Grey along the lakeshore trail (approx. 11km, 3–4 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Grey — a spectacularly situated refugio with direct views of the glacier across the lake. Enjoy the hot showers (available for a small fee at most refugios) and celebrate nearing the end of the W Trek.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande before kayak departure — eggs, toast, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the kayak or brief stop on shore — energy-dense snacks and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Set dinner at Refugio Grey — warm stew, bread, and dessert with glacier views. Budget ~$25–30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking expedition must be booked in advance through Lago Grey operator or your boutique stay concierge. Waterproof gear and gloves are provided but bring an extra warm layer. The icebergs glow an ethereal blue — one of the most otherworldly experiences in Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Wake early at Refugio Grey and hike back eastward along the lakeshore trail to Refugio Paine Grande (approx. 11km, 3 hours). This return section offers fresh perspectives on the glacier and mountains with morning light. Catch the scheduled catamaran across Lago Pehoé back toward the park's central area (catamaran departs at set times — confirm schedule, typically 9am and 12pm in peak season).
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer by park shuttle or private vehicle from the catamaran dock to your boutique accommodation in the W Circuit / Lago del Toro area. Check in, shower, unpack, and breathe — the W Trek is complete! Spend the afternoon resting, doing laundry, and enjoying the comfort of your boutique stay after 4 nights on the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the W Trek with a proper sit-down dinner. Enjoy the boutique stay's facilities — lounge area, views, and any on-site amenities. Reflect on the week's extraordinary landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final refugio breakfast at Grey — porridge, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Snack at Paine Grande while waiting for catamaran, or packed lunch on the boat
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at your boutique stay's restaurant or a nearby mid-range restaurant — Patagonian lamb asado or grilled trout. Budget ~$30–40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The catamaran crossing of Lago Pehoé is a beautiful finale to the W Trek with views of the Cuernos reflected in the water. Confirm catamaran times the evening before at Paine Grande. Your boutique stay may offer luggage storage — arrange this before the trek so fresh clothes await your return.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day at your boutique accommodation. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast with views of the park. Take a gentle, flat walk around the nearby lagoons (Laguna Verde or Laguna Azul are accessible from the central park area) — easy 2–3km strolls with excellent birdwatching for flamingos, black-necked swans, and upland geese.
day_by_day.afternoon: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari — join an expert naturalist guide for a dedicated afternoon wildlife tracking excursion through the park's open pampas and lenga beech forests (typically 3–4 hours, pre-booked, ~$80–120 USD per person). Search for pumas, guanacos, foxes, and rheas with high-powered binoculars and a guide skilled in reading animal signs and tracks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay as the long summer evening light bathes the landscape golden. Enjoy a sundowner drink on the terrace watching for condors and guanacos on the hillside.

meals.breakfast: Full leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh bread, eggs, local jams, coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the boutique stay or packed snacks during the wildlife safari
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique stay's restaurant — try the king crab (centolla) if available, or Patagonian lamb. Budget ~$30–40 USD.

day_by_day.notes: December is an excellent month for puma sightings in Torres del Paine — the park has one of the highest densities of pumas in the world and they are increasingly accustomed to vehicles and guided groups. Early morning and late afternoon are prime viewing times. Bring binoculars.

day_by_day.morning: Day hike to Mirador Ferrier — a less-crowded trail that rewards with sweeping panoramic views of Lago Pehoé, the Paine Massif, and the Grey Glacier from above. The hike is approximately 14km round-trip with 600m elevation gain and takes 5–6 hours total. Depart early from the boutique stay with a packed lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Mirador Ferrier and return to the boutique stay by mid-afternoon. Spend time in the late afternoon exploring the shoreline of Lago del Toro — the park's largest lake — watching for black-necked swans and Magellanic woodpeckers in the surrounding forest.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the park's CONAF administration center at Lago del Toro (if open) for natural history exhibits about the park's geology, flora, and fauna. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before the day hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mirador Ferrier summit — sandwiches, fruit, chocolate
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the park's Lago del Toro area or at the boutique stay — grilled lamb chops with local potato and chimichurri. Budget ~$25–35 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Mirador Ferrier is a rewarding alternative for those who want panoramic views without the W Trek crowds. The trail can be muddy after rain — waterproof boots essential. Start early to avoid afternoon winds which can be intense on exposed ridgelines.

day_by_day.morning: Horseback riding excursion through the park's open pampas — arrange through your boutique stay or a local outfitter (typically $80–100 USD for 3–4 hours). Ride through guanaco-dotted grasslands with the Paine Massif as a backdrop, experiencing the park the way Patagonian gauchos have for generations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the horse ride and enjoy a relaxed afternoon at the boutique stay. Take a short walk to the Salto Grande waterfall — a powerful cascade connecting Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoé, just minutes from the main park hub. The roar of the falls and the turquoise water rushing through a narrow canyon is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography session at Laguna Amarga — one of the park's most photogenic spots with pink flamingos wading in the mineral-rich waters and the Torres del Paine towers rising dramatically in the background.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Hostería Pehoé restaurant near Salto Grande — mid-range lake-view dining with sandwiches, soups, and local craft beer. Budget ~$15–20 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique stay — enjoy a set menu with Patagonian specialties. Budget ~$30–40 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Horseback riding must be booked at least 24 hours in advance. Wear long pants and closed-toe shoes. Salto Grande is accessible by a short 10-minute walk from the main parking area and is one of the most visited spots in the park — visit late afternoon to avoid tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the northern sector of the park — hire a park shuttle or join a guided day tour to Lago Azul and Laguna Azul, the park's most remote and least-visited lakes. The northern pampas offer exceptional guanaco and rhea viewing and a completely different, more open landscape than the W Trek corridor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the northern circuit exploration with a stop at Mirador Lago Azul for sweeping views of the impossibly blue lake framed by the Monte Almirante Nieto range. Return to the boutique stay by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve — enjoy a special festive dinner at the boutique stay, which typically organizes a celebratory meal in December. Toast to an extraordinary week in one of the world's most spectacular national parks.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before the northern sector day trip
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch at Laguna Azul shore — prepare with supplies from the boutique stay kitchen or park shop
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at the boutique stay — expect a festive set menu with Patagonian lamb, seafood, and local wines. Budget ~$40–55 USD per person for the holiday meal.

day_by_day.notes: The northern sector of Torres del Paine sees far fewer visitors than the W Trek corridor and offers a more authentic wilderness experience. The road to Laguna Azul requires a 4WD vehicle — confirm transportation with the boutique stay. This is a wonderful area for puma tracking as well.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — a slow, celebratory morning. Sleep in and enjoy a special holiday breakfast at the boutique stay. Take a leisurely morning walk to Mirador Condor — a short 1-hour hike from the main park hub with reliable Andean condor sightings as the massive birds ride morning thermals above the valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon in Torres del Paine — spend it exactly as you wish. Options include: returning to a favorite viewpoint for last photographs, a relaxed kayak or stand-up paddleboard session on Lago del Toro (if offered by the boutique stay), reading in the lounge with mountain views, or a final gentle walk through the lenga beech forest listening to Magellanic woodpeckers.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the boutique stay. Pack your bags for the morning transfer. Step outside one final time to take in the night sky — Patagonia offers some of the darkest skies in the Southern Hemisphere, and December nights reveal the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds in extraordinary clarity.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh pastries, eggs, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the boutique stay — soup, salad, and local bread
meals.dinner: Farewell Christmas dinner at the boutique stay — a memorable final meal with Patagonian lamb or fresh trout, local Carménère or Malbec wine, and dessert. Budget ~$35–45 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Take time this evening to tip your guides and refugio staff if you haven't already — tipping is appreciated in Chilean Patagonia. Download or back up all your photographs. Check the boutique stay's checkout time and arrange your morning transfer to Puerto Natales.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake early for one last sunrise over the Paine Massif from the boutique stay's terrace. Enjoy a full farewell breakfast. Check out and board your pre-arranged transfer to Puerto Natales (approx. 1.5–2.5 hours depending on your boutique stay location within the park).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Puerto Natales with time for a final stroll along the waterfront, last-minute souvenir shopping (local wool products, pisco, Chilean wine, and Patagonian artisan crafts make excellent gifts), and a proper sit-down farewell lunch before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Punta Arenas airport or Puerto Natales airstrip for onward flights. Depart Patagonia with memories of granite towers, blue glaciers, thundering waterfalls, pumas on the pampas, and one of the most extraordinary trekking experiences on Earth.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at the boutique stay before checkout
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch in Puerto Natales at La Mesita Grande — beloved local pizzeria and restaurant with excellent mid-range prices. Budget ~$15–20 USD. Or try Singular Puerto Natales bar for a more upscale farewell drink and light meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the transfer from Torres del Paine to Punta Arenas airport — roads can be unpredictable and border crossings (if routing through Argentina) add time. Confirm your transfer booking the evening before. The 12-day Torres del Paine experience — from the W Trek to glacier kayaking, wildlife safaris, and sunrise at the towers — represents one of the world's truly bucket-list adventures.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: W Circuit, Torres del Paine National Park Boutique Stay
hotel.location: W Circuit, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route that winds through the most spectacular landscapes of Torres del Paine, including the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the base of the iconic Torres towers. Stay in mountain refugios or camp along the way for a true Patagonian adventure.
experiences.location: W Circuit, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Set out before dawn to hike to the base of the three iconic granite towers of Torres del Paine. Arrive at the glacial lagoon at sunrise to witness the towers bathed in golden and pink light reflecting off the turquoise water — one of the most breathtaking natural spectacles in South America.
experiences.location: Mirador Las Torres, Eastern Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the stunning blue ice walls of one of Patagonia's most impressive glaciers, offering a unique perspective impossible to get on foot.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Grey Glacier Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Trekking Day
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, towering granite walls, and the peaks of Cuernos del Paine. Listen for the thunderous crack of ice avalanches cascading down the mountainsides as you trek through this awe-inspiring natural amphitheater.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari
experiences.description: Join an expert naturalist guide on a dedicated wildlife tracking excursion through the park's open pampas and valleys. Torres del Paine is one of the best places on Earth to spot wild pumas, guanacos, Andean condors, and rheas in their natural habitat. Early morning and dusk offer the highest chances of sightings.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Pampas, Northern Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport to your boutique lodge in the W Circuit area of Torres del Paine National Park. Enjoy panoramic Patagonian steppe scenery en route. Upon arrival, receive a personalized welcome with a pisco sour and orientation briefing from your dedicated guide. Settle into your premium suite and take a leisurely walk around the lodge grounds to acclimatize and absorb the first views of the Paine Massif.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive welcome dinner at the lodge's fine-dining restaurant featuring locally sourced Patagonian lamb, king crab, and regional wines from the Maipo and Colchagua valleys. Meet your private guide team and receive a detailed briefing on the 12-day program, gear check, and weather assessment.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light gourmet snack box provided during private transfer, featuring artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the lodge restaurant: slow-roasted Patagonian lamb with chimichurri, king crab bisque, quinoa salad with native herbs, and a curated Chilean wine pairing from a premium sommelier selection

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking gear is laid out for inspection this evening. The lodge concierge will provide a weather forecast and adjust the following days' schedule if needed. Altitude and wind acclimatization begins immediately — drink plenty of water and rest well.

day_by_day.morning: Guided orientation hike around the lodge's immediate surroundings — a 2–3 hour moderate trail offering sweeping views of Lago del Toro and the southern Paine Massif. Your private naturalist guide introduces local flora, Patagonian steppe ecology, and bird species including Andean condors and upland geese. Perfect warm-up hike to calibrate fitness and footwear before the main trekking days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari in the open pampas and lenga beech forests near the park's southern sector. An expert tracker guides your small group (maximum 4 guests) using telemetry data and field signs to locate pumas, guanacos, foxes, and rheas. Luxury 4WD vehicle with elevated viewing platforms and premium optics provided.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the lodge's panoramic terrace watching the alpenglow paint the granite towers gold and crimson. Private stargazing session with a telescope guided by an astronomy expert, taking advantage of Patagonia's exceptionally dark skies in December.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet lodge breakfast: freshly baked medialunas, smoked salmon, scrambled eggs with native herbs, seasonal fruit, artisan granola, and premium single-origin coffee and loose-leaf teas
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the trail — insulated hamper with quinoa and roasted vegetable salad, empanadas, Patagonian cheese board, dark chocolate, and thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant: pan-seared Patagonian trout with capers and lemon butter, roasted root vegetables, and a dessert of calafate berry tart with crème fraîche; paired with a crisp Casablanca Valley Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed but December is an excellent month for puma activity as cubs are young and mothers are frequently visible. Bring layered clothing — Patagonian weather can shift from warm sunshine to cold wind within minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn departure (04:30) for the iconic Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Your private guide leads you by headlamp along the well-marked trail through lenga beech forest, ascending the moraine to arrive at the turquoise glacial lake at the base of the three granite towers precisely at first light. Witness the towers ignite in shades of amber and rose — one of Patagonia's most breathtaking spectacles. Champagne toast at the mirador.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend at a relaxed pace, pausing for photography and flora identification. Return to the lodge by early afternoon for a restorative hot shower and spa treatment — choose from a deep-tissue massage, calafate berry scrub, or hydrotherapy session at the lodge's premium wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef's table dinner experience — a 6-course tasting menu prepared tableside by the head chef, featuring the best of Patagonian land and sea: sea urchin ceviche, Magellanic mussel chowder, guanaco tartare, Patagonian lamb rack, and a calafate and pisco soufflé. Paired with a curated vertical wine flight.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy breakfast at 04:00: overnight oats with dried fruit, energy bars, hard-boiled eggs, and vacuum flask of premium coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike brunch at the lodge: avocado toast with poached eggs and smoked trout, fresh-pressed juices, and a restorative bone broth
meals.dinner: Private chef's table 6-course tasting menu with full wine pairing — the lodge's signature premium dining experience

day_by_day.notes: This is the most iconic hike of the entire trip. Weather permitting, clear December mornings offer the best photography conditions. Your guide carries emergency gear, satellite communication, and a full first-aid kit. The round-trip hike is approximately 18–20 km and 800 m elevation gain — a rewarding but demanding full-day effort.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest morning — optional gentle yoga session on the lodge's outdoor deck overlooking the lake, led by a resident instructor. Alternatively, enjoy a leisurely breakfast and browse the lodge's curated library of Patagonian natural history and photography books. Visit the on-site gear boutique to acquire any additional equipment for the upcoming W Trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Introductory Valle del Francés sector exploration — a private guided half-day hike into the lower valley to preview the landscape before the full trekking day. Observe hanging glaciers on the flanks of Paine Grande and the dramatic rock amphitheater of Cuernos del Paine. Return by private catamaran across Lago Pehoé for a scenic water-level perspective of the massif.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive wine and cheese pairing event hosted by the lodge sommelier — featuring six premium Chilean and Argentine wines matched with artisan Patagonian cheeses, house-cured meats, and wild mushroom crostini. Informal and educational atmosphere on the fireside lounge.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast: eggs Benedict with Patagonian ham, fresh-squeezed orange juice, pastry basket, and a coffee tasting flight of three single-origin roasts
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch: Patagonian lamb and quinoa soup, sourdough bread, and a seasonal green salad with native berry vinaigrette
meals.dinner: Fireside dinner at the lodge: slow-braised Patagonian beef short rib with smoked paprika polenta, roasted beet salad, and a warm calafate berry crumble with vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Today is a strategic rest and preview day before the multi-day W Trek begins. Use this afternoon to confirm all gear is packed, boots are broken in, and any blisters or discomfort are addressed with the lodge's in-house physiotherapist.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 1 — Departure from the lodge toward the Lago Grey sector. Private transfer to the Grey trailhead. Begin trekking north along the western arm of the W, through ancient lenga beech forest and open ridgelines with dramatic views of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Your private guide narrates the glaciological and geological history of the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to the Grey Glacier viewpoint — one of the most awe-inspiring sights in all of Patagonia. The glacier's massive blue ice face stretches across the horizon, calving icebergs into the steel-grey lake. A private Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition launches from the shore: paddle among floating icebergs in sea kayaks with a specialist guide, reaching perspectives inaccessible on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a premium private camp or luxury refugio near Lago Grey, pre-arranged exclusively for your group. Camp staff have prepared a heated tent or private cabin, hot showers, and a fully catered dinner served under the stars. Campfire with a private guide storytelling session about Patagonian exploration history.

meals.breakfast: Pre-trek lodge breakfast: full hot buffet with protein-rich options, fresh fruit, and packed trail snacks for the day
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch on the glacier viewpoint: smoked salmon wraps, lentil salad, energy balls, hot soup from a thermos, and dark chocolate
meals.dinner: Private camp dinner: grilled Patagonian lamb chops, roasted garlic potatoes, mixed salad, and a warm chocolate fondant; Chilean red wine served by candlelight

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking on Lago Grey requires a minimum level of physical fitness and comfort on water. Dry suits and all safety equipment are provided. December offers long daylight hours (up to 17 hours of light), allowing a relaxed pace without time pressure.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Early morning hike from Grey camp toward Refugio Paine Grande, traversing the central section of the W. The trail offers continuous panoramic views of Lago Pehoé, the Cuernos del Paine, and the ice fields. Your guide identifies endemic plant species including the fire bush (notro) in full summer bloom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Paine Grande sector and begin the ascent into Valle del Francés — the dramatic centerpiece of the W Trek. Trek through the glacially carved valley with hanging glaciers on both sides, listening to the thunderous cracks of ice avalanches from the cliffs above. Reach the upper mirador for a 360-degree panorama of the massif.
day_by_day.evening: Descend and transfer by private catamaran across Lago Pehoé back to the main lodge for a luxury overnight recovery. Enjoy the lodge spa — hot tub, sauna, and massage — before a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: hot porridge with dried fruit and honey, scrambled eggs, Patagonian sausage, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch in Valle del Francés: grain salad with roasted vegetables, energy bars, nuts, and a thermos of hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant return dinner: pan-roasted Patagonian sea bass with saffron risotto and a calafate berry reduction; dessert of mille-feuille with pastry cream and fresh berries

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is the most visually dramatic section of the W Trek and should not be rushed. Allow extra time at the upper mirador for photography. The sound of ice avalanches is a natural and spectacular feature — your guide will ensure you are always in a safe viewing position.

day_by_day.morning: Full active rest day at the lodge — the longest day of the year in the Southern Hemisphere (summer solstice). Sleep in and enjoy a late, indulgent breakfast. Optional guided birdwatching walk on the lodge grounds and surrounding pampas, spotting Andean condors, black-necked swans, flamingos on nearby lagoons, and the elusive Magellanic woodpecker in the beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private photography workshop with a professional Patagonian landscape photographer — learn composition techniques, golden-hour shooting strategies, and how to capture the park's iconic subjects. The session includes a guided walk to a curated selection of viewpoints near the lodge for immediate practice.
day_by_day.evening: Solstice celebration dinner — a special themed menu created by the lodge chef to honor the longest day of the year. Guests dine on the outdoor terrace (heated with fire pits and blankets) as the sun sets after 22:00, casting extraordinary light across the towers. Live acoustic guitar performance by a local Patagonian musician.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast: full lodge buffet with made-to-order omelets, smoked fish, fresh pastries, and freshly blended fruit smoothies
meals.lunch: Lodge terrace lunch: grilled vegetables and halloumi, Patagonian shrimp ceviche, sourdough bread, and sparkling water with fresh herbs
meals.dinner: Solstice celebration 5-course dinner on the terrace: king crab and avocado tostada, Patagonian lamb consommé, grilled Angus tenderloin with truffle butter, artisan cheese selection, and a calafate berry pavlova; premium Champagne welcome toast

day_by_day.notes: December 21 is the summer solstice — sunset occurs around 22:15 in Torres del Paine, making this an extraordinary evening for photography and outdoor dining. Warm layers are essential even in summer as temperatures drop quickly after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — The final and most celebrated leg: the hike to Mirador Las Torres from the western approach via the Valle Ascencio. Depart early to beat the crowds and hike through lenga beech forest, crossing wooden bridges over glacial streams. Your guide shares stories of the first climbers to scale the towers in the 1960s.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the glacial moraine and ascend to the iconic mirador for a second visit — this time in full afternoon light with a different atmospheric quality. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch at the base of the towers, with the turquoise lake reflecting the granite spires. Descend at leisure, completing the W Trek circuit.
day_by_day.evening: W Trek completion celebration — a private ceremony at the lodge with a personalized certificate, commemorative gift, and a congratulatory Champagne toast with your guide team. The lodge chef prepares a special celebratory dinner in your honor.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast: high-protein start with eggs, quinoa porridge, smoked meats, and trail snacks packed for the hike
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic at Mirador Las Torres: artisan sandwiches with Patagonian ham and aged cheese, fresh fruit, brownies, and a thermos of hot tea
meals.dinner: W Trek completion dinner: whole roasted Patagonian lamb (asado al palo), grilled seasonal vegetables, chimichurri, sopaipillas, and a dessert of tres leches cake; toasted with a magnum of premium Carménère

day_by_day.notes: Completing the W Trek is a significant physical achievement. Your guide will arrange for your trekking boots to be cleaned and conditioned by lodge staff overnight. A physiotherapy recovery session is available upon return to the lodge — book in advance with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury recovery day — sleep as late as desired. Indulge in a premium spa morning: 90-minute deep-tissue sports massage, calafate berry body wrap, and a private hot tub session overlooking the Paine Massif. The lodge's in-house physiotherapist is available for targeted muscle recovery treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided fly-fishing excursion on one of the premium private estancias bordering the national park. Fish for brown and rainbow trout in crystal-clear Patagonian rivers with a certified guide. All equipment provided; catch-and-release practice observed. Non-fishing guests may accompany and enjoy a private picnic on the riverbank.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-Christmas Eve celebration dinner — the lodge's culinary team prepares a festive Patagonian feast with traditional and modern influences. Guests gather in the main fireside dining room for a communal yet intimate experience.

meals.breakfast: Late, indulgent breakfast served in-room or on your private balcony: eggs any style, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit platter, and a Bloody Mary or fresh juice of your choice
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic during fly-fishing: gourmet charcuterie board, Patagonian cheese, crusty bread, pickles, and a chilled bottle of Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Pre-Christmas dinner: Patagonian king crab legs with drawn butter, slow-roasted pork belly with apple and fennel, roasted root vegetables, and a yule log cake with calafate berry coulis; mulled wine and artisan pisco cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Fly-fishing in Patagonia requires a Chilean fishing license, which the lodge concierge arranges in advance on your behalf. December is peak season for brown trout — conditions are typically excellent. Bring sun protection as the Patagonian sun is intense at this latitude.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve private wildlife and landscape photography drive through the park's northern sector — areas less frequented by trekkers. Your expert guide and photographer companion lead a 4WD expedition to remote viewpoints of the Paine Massif, Lago Nordenskjöld, and the Cuernos del Paine from unique angles. High probability of guanaco and condor sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a leisurely afternoon. Optional: private catamaran cruise on Lago Pehoé with Champagne and canapés, gliding beneath the Cuernos del Paine and Paine Grande for unrivaled photographic perspectives. Alternatively, relax in the lodge library or enjoy the hot tub as the afternoon light transforms the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner — the lodge's signature annual event. A lavish multi-course feast in the beautifully decorated dining room with candlelight, festive décor incorporating native Patagonian botanicals, and live classical guitar music. Guests are invited to dress for the occasion.

meals.breakfast: Christmas Eve breakfast: smoked salmon blinis, scrambled eggs with truffle, freshly baked croissants, and a glass of sparkling cava
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch: Patagonian shrimp tacos with avocado crema, fresh slaw, and lime; sparkling water and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala 7-course dinner: oysters on ice, lobster bisque, sea urchin pasta, Patagonian lamb tenderloin with rosemary jus, artisan cheese trolley, calafate berry sorbet, and a dark chocolate and hazelnut bûche de Noël; full premium wine pairing and a midnight Champagne toast

day_by_day.notes: The Christmas Eve Gala Dinner is a highlight of the lodge calendar. Smart-casual or elegant attire is recommended. The lodge decorates with native lenga beech branches, calafate berries, and candlelight for a uniquely Patagonian festive atmosphere. Gift-wrapping service available through the concierge for any locally purchased souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning sunrise hike to a private viewpoint above the lodge — a short 45-minute guided walk to a ridge with panoramic views of the entire southern Paine Massif. Your guide carries a thermos of hot chocolate and a small gift from the lodge team. Return for a leisurely Christmas brunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari — a dedicated 4-hour afternoon expedition into the park's most productive wildlife corridors. December is an exceptional month for puma sightings as cubs born in September are becoming active. Your expert tracker uses field signs, camera traps, and telemetry to maximize sighting probability. A truly once-in-a-lifetime wildlife experience.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas farewell dinner — a relaxed, joyful celebration of the journey completed. The lodge team joins guests for a toast, and the chef presents a final Patagonian feast. Gift exchange of locally made artisan products: native wool textiles, pisco, calafate berry preserves, and a custom photo book of your trip prepared by the lodge photography team.

meals.breakfast: Christmas brunch: Eggs Benedict royale with smoked salmon and hollandaise, fresh-pressed juices, a Champagne mimosa, pastry selection, and a fruit and berry platter
meals.lunch: Light afternoon snack before safari: artisan empanadas, fresh fruit, and herbal tea
meals.dinner: Christmas farewell dinner: whole roasted Patagonian lamb (the lodge's signature asado), grilled king crab, wood-fired vegetables, sopaipillas with pebre, and a grand dessert table of traditional Chilean sweets and calafate berry ice cream; premium pisco sours and a curated wine selection from the lodge cellar

day_by_day.notes: The custom photo book is a complimentary gift prepared by the lodge's in-house photography team using images captured throughout your stay — arrange final image submissions by mid-afternoon. Pack and prepare luggage this evening for the following morning's departure transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the lodge — a leisurely last breakfast with panoramic views of the Paine Massif. Take a final short walk around the lodge grounds to photograph and absorb the landscape one last time. Personal farewell from the guide team and lodge management. Private luxury transfer departs for Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer through the Patagonian steppe — a scenic 3–4 hour journey with one final stop at a panoramic viewpoint for a last photograph of the Torres del Paine. Your guide accompanies you to the airport and assists with luggage and check-in formalities. Onward flight departs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 12 extraordinary days in one of the world's last great wildernesses. The lodge concierge provides a curated selection of Patagonian artisan gifts, a bottle of premium pisco, and a handwritten farewell note to enjoy on your journey home.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast: full hot buffet, freshly baked pastries, smoked fish, made-to-order eggs, and a final cup of premium Patagonian coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet departure snack box for the transfer: artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, Patagonian chocolate, and sparkling water — prepared by the lodge kitchen
meals.dinner: Onboard or at departure airport — lodge concierge can recommend premium dining options in Punta Arenas if a layover permits

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details with the lodge concierge 48 hours in advance to ensure the transfer timing is optimal. Allow extra time at Punta Arenas airport as international connections may require early check-in. The lodge's concierge team remains available by WhatsApp for any post-departure assistance or future booking inquiries.
